correctness.rationale: In the closed code-generated shift, binary factors come from single gaps and all even-shift words extend to arbitrarily long allowed gaps. Thus the marker-free subsystem is exactly the even shift; pointing one marker in a labeled n-window gives n/k times the tuple count for k blocks even when the least period divides n. The language Fibonacci count and trace correction for all-zero orbits give the stated W and the factor (1+z)/(1−z−z²). Positive coefficients and code lengths 2 and 3 give a unique simple dominant pole r, since equality in the triangle inequality forces both phases one. The logarithmic derivative after removing that pole is holomorphic on a larger disk, giving the strict exponential error, and divisor inversion gives the orbit asymptotic. The word-count renewal bound and periodic lower bound establish the already known entropy identity. At the dense dyadic directions, the dominant Binet component is unbounded but grows at most logarithmically along the radius (split at 2^j≈1/(1−t)), so it cannot be meromorphic there; the other Binet components are analytic through the circle. The meromorphic quotient identity transfers the obstruction to the zeta function, notwithstanding the smaller Taylor radius. The separate exact-rational bracket and n=1–10 cyclic enumeration agree with the original support, and evaluation of the displayed series gives r≈0.442107675333 and 1/r≈2.261892420770.
residual_risks: The finite counts and rational bracket do not certify any all-period claim or boundary; those follow from the exact counting and analytic arguments. Nonsoficity, typical periodic optimization and the entropy equation are existing results, not new in this record.
